```{r setup}
res <- file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "results")
rd <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(res, f), check.names = FALSE)
prof <- rd("profile-lf.csv"); names(prof)[5] <- "ops"
cand <- rbind(rd("candidates-opaka.csv"), rd("candidates-io_yft.csv"))
wf <- rbind(rd("candidates-wf-opaka.csv"), rd("candidates-wf-io_yft.csv"))
dyn <- rbind(rd("candidates-dyn-opaka.csv"), rd("candidates-dyn-io_yft.csv"))
ad <- rd("ad-safety.csv")
fits <- rbind(rd("fits-opaka-lf.csv"), rd("fits-io_yft-lf.csv"))
tim <- rd("timing.csv")
tests <- list(original = rd("opal-tests-original.csv"),
              `atomic product` = rd("opal-tests-lf-atomic_product.csv"),
              `atomic product + block rebin + identity skip` = rd("opal-tests-lf-atomic_product_block_skip.csv"))
case_lab <- c(opaka = "Opakapaka", io_yft = "IO yellowfin (AGE-SF)")
sci <- function(x) ifelse(x == 0, "0", formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1))
med <- function(cs, kind, v, col) median(tim[tim$case == cs & tim$kind == kind & tim$version == v, col], na.rm = TRUE)
pr <- function(cs, st, col, tp = "default") prof[prof$case == cs & prof$stage == st & prof$tape == tp, col]
```

## Question

Where inside opal's length-composition likelihood and population dynamics
does a gradient call spend its time, and can that time be reduced without
changing the model's numeric output or the ability to estimate any parameter?
Weight compositions share the length code's structure, so changes there are
tested for both.

## Setup

* opal `dev` at `87c5494`, RTMB 2.0, R 4.6.2 (opal's tests: R 4.5.2, which
  has testthat; same opal source). One cloud container, one thread.
* Models: the Opakapaka quickstart fit (82 length rows, legacy bin pooling,
  44 ages, 17 length bins) and the IO yellowfin article model AGE-SF (1,241
  length rows in two composition schemes, 28 ages, 39 length bins, 20
  fisheries, 256 quarterly steps), rebuilt from the fits stored in opal.
* Candidate versions of `get_length_like()`, `get_weight_like()` and
  `do_dynamics()` were swapped into the installed opal namespace; opal itself
  was not modified.
* Neither model has weight compositions. Each model's length data were also
  supplied as weight-composition data (same observations, bins and schemes;
  identity length-to-weight matrix for the legacy path), which reproduces the
  length objective exactly (`r sum(wf$wf_equals_lf, na.rm = TRUE)` of 2).
* Parameter vectors used in the checks: the stored estimate, the stored start
  and the jittered starts of `benchmarks/nlminb-r46` (20 Opakapaka, 10 IO
  yellowfin).

## Profile

`get_length_like()` was cut after each step, returning the sum of everything
computed so far, with the rest of the model unchanged. "None" is the model
without the length likelihood.

```{r profile}
p <- prof[prof$stage != 4, ]
p$step[p$stage == 0] <- "none (rest of the model)"
p$step[p$stage == 99] <- "full length likelihood"
w <- reshape(p[, c("case", "tape", "stage", "step", "ops", "gr_ms")], idvar = c("case", "stage", "step"),
             timevar = "tape", direction = "wide")
w <- w[order(match(w$case, c("opaka", "io_yft")), w$stage), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = case_lab[w$case], `Cumulative to` = w$step,
                        `Tape ops` = w$ops.default, `gr (ms)` = w$gr_ms.default,
                        `Tape ops, atomic matmul` = w$ops.atomic, `gr (ms), atomic matmul` = w$gr_ms.atomic,
                        check.names = FALSE),
             digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Cumulative cost at each step, at the stored estimate. Single measurements (medians of 5 blocks of calls); run-to-run variation in this container is about 10-20%.")
```

* With opal's default tape, almost all of the length likelihood's cost is
  the product of predicted catch-at-age and the probability-of-length-at-age
  matrix (`catch_ya %*% t(pla)`, one product per fishery). For IO yellowfin it
  adds `r format(pr("io_yft", 1, "ops") - pr("io_yft", 0, "ops"), big.mark = ",")`
  of `r format(pr("io_yft", 99, "ops"), big.mark = ",")` tape operations and
  about `r round(pr("io_yft", 1, "gr_ms") - pr("io_yft", 0, "gr_ms"))` of
  `r round(pr("io_yft", 99, "gr_ms"))` ms of the gradient. RTMB tapes it as
  one multiply and one add per element. `pla` is an AD object on the tape
  even when growth is fixed.
* The per-row rebinning products add no operations with the default tape.
  1,114 of the 1,241 IO yellowfin rows use a 39 × 39 identity matrix and the
  other 127 a 0/1 pooling matrix.
* `RTMB::TapeConfig(atomic = "enable")` (atomic matrix products everywhere)
  makes the catch × PLA product cheap but turns the 1,241 rebinning products
  into atomic operations whose cost replaces the saving, which is why the
  atomic tape barely changed the IO yellowfin gradient in
  `benchmarks/optimizers`.
* Everything outside the length likelihood costs about
  `r round(pr("io_yft", 0, "gr_ms"), 1)` ms of the IO yellowfin gradient.
  The earlier profile in `benchmarks/optimizers` attributed most of the
  non-composition cost to the dynamics; that came from cut tapes that keep
  quantities the full model discards, and overstated it.

## Candidates

| Candidate | Change |
|---|---|
| refactor | length and weight likelihoods through one shared function; no other change |
| atomic_product | the catch × PLA product taped as one atomic matrix product (`TapeConfig(list(matmul = "atomic"))` around that product only, previous setting restored) |
| block_rebin | rebinning with one product per fishery and scheme instead of one per row |
| skip_identity | no rebinning product when a scheme's matrix is the identity (decided from data) |
| atomic_all | block rebinning also taped as atomic |
| vec | add the constant and normalise a whole block at once |

The density is evaluated row by row on the original observation vectors in
every candidate, and the REPORT items keep their names and shapes.

```{r candidates}
show <- function(d, extra = NULL) {
  d <- d[d$candidate != "original", ]
  data.frame(Model = case_lab[d$case], Candidate = d$candidate,
             `fn identical` = d$fn_identical, `fn max rel. diff` = sci(d$fn_max_rel),
             `gr max scaled diff` = sci(d$gr_max_scaled), `REPORT max rel. diff` = sci(d$report_max_rel),
             `Hessian max rel. diff` = sci(d$he_max_rel), `Tape ops` = format(d$tape, big.mark = ","),
             `gr (ms)` = d$gr_ms, check.names = FALSE)
}
base_gr <- function(d) setNames(d$gr_ms[d$candidate == "original"], d$case[d$candidate == "original"])
knitr::kable(show(cand), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Length compositions. Differences over the stored estimate, start 0 and all jittered starts; Hessian at the stored estimate. Gradient differences are scaled by 1 + the gradient's largest element (the gradient is about 1e-11 at the stored estimate). Original gr: Opakapaka %.2f ms, IO yellowfin %.1f ms (single measurements).", base_gr(cand)[["opaka"]], base_gr(cand)[["io_yft"]]))
```

* The shared-function refactor reproduces the original exactly.
* The atomic catch × PLA product alone gives almost all of the saving. The
  objective is bit-identical for IO yellowfin and differs by one rounding unit
  for Opakapaka; gradients, REPORT items and Hessians agree to rounding
  (largest scaled gradient difference
  `r sci(max(cand$gr_max_scaled))`; absolute
  `r sci(max(cand$gr_max_abs))`). The Hessian stays positive definite.
* Block rebinning, the identity skip, atomic rebinning and block
  normalisation change times by up to about 10% on top of that, within the
  run-to-run variation of single measurements.

```{r wf}
knitr::kable(show(wf), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Weight compositions (the models' length data supplied as weight compositions), same checks. Original gr: Opakapaka %.2f ms, IO yellowfin %.1f ms.", base_gr(wf)[["opaka"]], base_gr(wf)[["io_yft"]]))
```

The weight-composition likelihood behaves the same way, on both its scheme
path (IO yellowfin) and its legacy path (Opakapaka).

## Dynamics

The candidate replaces the per-fishery loops inside each year and season of
`do_dynamics()` with matrix operations over the fisheries with catch in that
step, with the sums over ages taped as scalar operations ("plain", same order
of summation) or as atomic products.

```{r dyn}
knitr::kable(show(dyn), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Dynamics candidate alone and with the length candidate 'lf_best' (atomic product + block rebinning + identity skip). Original gr: Opakapaka %.2f ms, IO yellowfin %.1f ms.", base_gr(dyn)[["opaka"]], base_gr(dyn)[["io_yft"]]))
```

The vectorised dynamics change the tape size by up to 9% (atomic sums with
the length candidate) and less than 3% otherwise. The gradient times above
are single measurements; their differences are of the size of the run-to-run
variation (10-20%) and not consistent in direction across the two models, so
no gain is shown. Everything outside the length likelihood is about 3 ms of
the IO yellowfin gradient, which bounds what the dynamics could save.

## Estimating every parameter

Any fixed parameter could be estimated, so each candidate was also compared
with the original with the map removed: growth, steepness, sigma_r, variance
terms, initial F and the fixed selectivity elements are then estimated, and
the PLA and weights are AD quantities (growth gradients non-zero:
`r all(ad$growth_gr_nonzero)`).

```{r ad}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = case_lab[ad$case], Candidate = ad$candidate, Parameters = ad$n_par,
                        `fn identical` = ad$fn_identical, `fn max rel. diff` = sci(ad$fn_max_rel),
                        `gr max scaled diff` = sci(ad$gr_max_scaled), `gr max abs. diff` = sci(ad$gr_max_abs),
                        check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Objective and gradient with every parameter estimated, at the stored estimate (fixed values at their stored values), start 0 and the jittered starts. lf_atomic_product, lf_best and lf_atomic_all are the length candidates atomic_product, atomic_product_block_skip and atomic_all_block_skip.")
```

The first version of the dynamics candidate failed this check: `matrix()` on
an AD vector drops RTMB's class. It passed after indexing was used instead,
and the results above are from that version.

## opal's tests

```{r tests}
tt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tests), function(n) { d <- tests[[n]]
  data.frame(Functions = n, Tests = nrow(d), Expectations = sum(d$nb), Failed = sum(d$failed),
             Errors = sum(d$error), Skipped = sum(d$skipped)) }))
knitr::kable(tt, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "opal's tests of the affected code (likelihoods, schemes, weight compositions, OSA residuals, simulation, dynamics, gradients, quickstart and regression tests; 18 files), with the length and weight candidates swapped in.")
```

* The one error occurs with the original functions as well: the stored
  Opakapaka fit fails its runtime identity check in this container ("The saved
  fit runtime identity does not match its payload").
* The first run of the candidates failed 85 expectations in the simulation and
  OSA tests, although every objective, gradient and Hessian check had passed.
  RTMB's `OBS()` registers an observation under the text of its argument
  (`deparse(substitute(x))`); the shared function called it on a renamed copy
  (`obs_flat`), so `obj$simulate()` and `oneStepPredict()` could not find
  `lf_obs_flat`. Calling `OBS()` on the original names in the exported
  functions fixed it. Any refactor that moves the composition code into a
  shared helper has to keep this.

## Fits and timing

```{r fits}
o <- fits[fits$version == "original", ]; c1 <- fits[fits$version != "original", ]
m <- merge(o, c1, by = c("case", "start_id"), suffixes = c(".o", ".c"))
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(m, m$case), function(d) data.frame(
  Model = case_lab[d$case[1]], Starts = nrow(d),
  `Same objective (< 1e-6)` = sum(abs(d$objective.c - d$objective.o) < 1e-6),
  `Median time, original (s)` = median(d$elapsed_s.o), `Median time, atomic product (s)` = median(d$elapsed_s.c),
  `Median gr calls, original` = median(d$gr_evals.o), `Median gr calls, atomic product` = median(d$gr_evals.c),
  `Max abs. parameter difference` = sci(max(d$max_par_diff.o)), check.names = FALSE))),
  digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "nlminb fits (opal defaults, 2 passes) with the original and the atomic-product length likelihood from the same starts, run back to back. Opakapaka: start 0 and all 20 jittered starts; IO yellowfin: start 0 and jittered starts 1, 3, 7 and 10.")
```

```{r timing}
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("opaka", "io_yft"), function(cs) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("lf", "wf"), function(k)
  data.frame(Model = case_lab[cs], Compositions = c(lf = "length", wf = "weight")[k],
             `fn original (ms)` = med(cs, k, "original", "fn_ms"), `fn candidate (ms)` = med(cs, k, "candidate", "fn_ms"),
             `gr original (ms)` = med(cs, k, "original", "gr_ms"), `gr candidate (ms)` = med(cs, k, "candidate", "gr_ms"),
             `Hessian original (ms)` = med(cs, k, "original", "he_ms"), `Hessian candidate (ms)` = med(cs, k, "candidate", "he_ms"),
             check.names = FALSE)))))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Paired timing at the stored estimate: medians of 6 alternating rounds (Hessian: 6 rounds for Opakapaka, 2 for IO yellowfin). Candidate: atomic catch x PLA product only.")
```

* Fits reached the same objective from every start, in
  `r round(100 * median(m$elapsed_s.c[m$case == "opaka"] / m$elapsed_s.o[m$case == "opaka"]))`%
  (Opakapaka) and
  `r round(100 * median(m$elapsed_s.c[m$case == "io_yft"] / m$elapsed_s.o[m$case == "io_yft"]))`%
  (IO yellowfin) of the original's time (median per start). Gradient counts
  differ by a few percent either way because the objective and gradient
  differ by rounding; parameter differences are at the scale where `nlminb`
  stops along the flat directions of these models.
* The gradient ranges of the 6 rounds do not overlap between versions for
  any model.

## Recommendation

Tape the catch × PLA product in `get_length_like()` and `get_weight_like()`
as an atomic matrix product, and change nothing else. In this study it cut
the IO yellowfin gradient and Hessian times to 35-40% and the Opakapaka times
to 45-55% of the original, kept the objective identical or within one
rounding unit, kept gradients, Hessians and REPORT output equal to rounding
in the stored models, kept objective and gradient equal to rounding with
every parameter estimated, and passed opal's tests. The other candidates added
little and are not needed now. The implementation plan is in
`issue-atomic-composition-products.md`.

## Limitations

* Two models, one machine, RTMB 2.0. The gain depends on the share of the gradient
  taken by the catch × PLA product (composition rows × ages × bins, relative
  to the rest of the model); it was not measured on other models. The BET model in opal's benchmark was not tested.
* "No change in numeric output" holds to rounding, not bit for bit: the
  atomic product sums in a different order. On models whose fits are
  sensitive to the start (IO yellowfin), rounding-level differences can send
  `nlminb` along a different path; in these fits they did not change any end
  point.
* The candidates were swapped into the installed package. A change inside
  opal still needs its own tests (listed in the implementation plan) and
  opal's benchmark.
* The switch uses RTMB's tape configuration, which is global state; it is
  restored after each product, including on error. Its availability in older
  RTMB versions was not checked.
* Weight compositions were tested with the models' length data supplied as
  weight compositions, not with real weight-composition data.

## Reproduce

```bash
export REFACTOR_DIR=benchmarks/gradient-refactor NLMINB_BENCH_DIR=benchmarks/nlminb-r46
R46=/opt/r462/bin/Rscript; R45=/opt/r452/bin/Rscript   # R 4.5.2 library has testthat
$R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/profile-lf.R
$R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-candidates.R
$R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-wf.R
$R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-dyn.R
$R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-ad-safety.R
for s in original lf; do LF_BEST=atomic_product $R45 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/run-opal-tests.R /path/to/opal $s; done
LF_BEST=atomic_product $R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-fits.R opaka lf
LF_BEST=atomic_product $R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/test-fits.R io_yft lf 0,1,3,7,10
LF_BEST=atomic_product $R46 --vanilla $REFACTOR_DIR/timing.R 6
quarto render benchmarks/gradient-refactor/gradient-refactor.qmd
```
